after: ## 4.1 Truman at home: ambition against obstruction
alt: Two columns. Passed: the Employment Act (1946), the Housing Act (1949), a minimum wage rise from 40 to 75 cents and wider Social Security (1950). Blocked: national health insurance, federal aid to education and the Brannan Plan, with Taft-Hartley passed over his veto. Below, the blockers: the AMA, a conservative coalition, the 1946 Republican Congress and the cost of Korea.
caption: Truman extended the New Deal, but his biggest proposals were blocked.

after: ## 4.1 Truman at home: ambition against obstruction
alt: A timeline from 1947 to 1954 drawn to scale: the Loyalty Program and HUAC (1947), the Soviet bomb (August 1949), China (October 1949), McCarthy's Wheeling speech (February 1950), Hiss's conviction (1950), Korea (June 1950), the Army-McCarthy hearings (1954) and censure (December 1954). Below, external and internal causes and the reasons for McCarthy's fall.
caption: The scare began with Truman's own measures, before McCarthy, and ended on television.

after: ## 4.1 Truman at home: ambition against obstruction
alt: A left-right line of the 1948 candidates: Wallace's Progressives, Truman, Dewey and Thurmond's Dixiecrats. A bar shows the electoral votes, Truman 303 to Dewey 189 (other candidates' votes not shown). Four reasons: the whistle-stop campaign, his coalition, his anti-communist record and Dewey's complacent campaign.
caption: Despite a three-way Democratic split, campaigning and coalition won Truman the election.

alt: A vertical timeline from 1946 to 1960 drawn to scale. Presidents and Congress on the left: To Secure These Rights (1947), Executive Order 9981 (July 1948), Little Rock and the weak Civil Rights Act (1957). Campaigners and courts on the right: Brown (1954), the Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955-56), the SCLC (1957) and the Greensboro sit-in and SNCC (1960).
caption: Presidents acted by executive order or under pressure; the movement and courts set the pace.

alt: Five drivers of consumer demand, wartime savings, the GI Bill, easy credit, defence spending and new technology, converge on a boom in cars, televisions, appliances and suburbs. Below, those left out: the rural poor, Black and Hispanic workers, unskilled non-union workers and women.
caption: The 1950s were prosperous, but not for everyone.

alt: A comparison table. Both presidents aimed at containment. Truman's methods were the Truman Doctrine, Marshall Aid, NATO and rearmament; Eisenhower's were nuclear deterrence and CIA coups. In Asia, Truman fought in Korea; Eisenhower backed Diem. Towards the USSR, Truman ran the Berlin airlift; Eisenhower sought peaceful coexistence until the U-2 incident.
caption: Same aim, different means: continuity in containment, change in method.
